subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should memory-triggered compaction runs delegate non-memory workspace writes to the normal write tool, or must they remain restricted to the single append-only memory target?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes what a silent housekeeping run may write, so automation should not pick the boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
options.body: Delegate writes outside the memory directory to the normal workspace/sandbox write tool while continuing to block other memory files and keeping append-only behavior for the planned target.

options.title: Keep strict single-target writes
options.body: Preserve the current security boundary and treat non-memory write attempts during memory flush as model/prompt failures that should be retried after compaction.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in mode
options.body: Keep the default strict but introduce a documented operator setting or approved runtime mode for trusted workflows that need broader writes during flush.

recommendation.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
recommendation.body: Delegate writes outside the memory directory to the normal workspace/sandbox write tool while continuing to block other memory files and keeping append-only behavior for the planned target.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced pre-compaction memory flush and is the best available routing candidate for the product/security boundary decision.
